principles: Political control is separate from settlement, route, fortification, and economic layers.
Later administrative boundaries are not promoted to 1326 political geometry.
Where sources disagree on exact conquest dates, retain the disagreement and lower confidence rather than inventing certainty.

evidence: Sakarya MEB district history states that Akcakoca brought the Sapanca Lake and Adapazari area into Ottoman control in 1324 and that Sapanca was taken in 1324-1326.
This is an institutional/local-history source and should be cross-checked before canonical promotion.
Sakarya University city-memory material attributes the early Ottoman conquest of Akyazi to Konur Alp.
Akyazi Chamber of Commerce records the general tradition that Konur Alp conquered Akyazi, Mudurnu and Konrapa during Osman/Orhan's expansion.
Exact 7 April 1326 boundary geometry is not established by these sources.
Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism states that Prusias ad Hypium was taken in 1323 by Konur Alp and incorporated into Ottoman territory.
The 2022 Turkish Historical Society journal article likewise dates incorporation to 1323 and identifies the settlement as continuing through the Byzantine and Ottoman periods.
The settlement had fortifications, a bridge and a strategic position near the Melen/Hypios river and routes toward Akcakoca and the Duzce plain.

The 2025 Sinop University research article reconstructs the 1304 Sakarya campaign using chronicles, archival evidence, maps and fieldwork, identifying Leblebici, Cadirli, Lefke, Mekece, Akhisar and Geyve as captured fortresses.
The article identifies the Lefke–Iznik road and associated watchpoints/fortifications, supporting a route-and-fortification model rather than a simple smooth political boundary.
A Duzce provincial educational publication describes Konur Alp's campaigns toward Akova and the Black Sea and his 1323 campaign around Bolu/Duzce.
The source also records Konur Alp's participation in the 1326 Bursa campaign and death in the same year; this supports his role in the regional conquest network but not an exact province boundary.

negativeOrCautionaryFindings.subject: Akova/Akyazi/Sapanca polygon
negativeOrCautionaryFindings.finding: Do not convert modern district boundaries or later Hüdavendigar/Kocaeli administrative limits into a 1326 political polygon.

negativeOrCautionaryFindings.subject: Konuralp extent
negativeOrCautionaryFindings.finding: The evidence establishes a settlement/control anchor, not the exact territorial extent of a Konur Alp domain.

negativeOrCautionaryFindings.subject: Ancient route continuity
negativeOrCautionaryFindings.finding: Ancient road evidence can support geographic plausibility but does not by itself prove uninterrupted medieval use in 1326.

runtimeImplications: Represent Sapanca, Akyazi and Konuralp as historical settlement/control anchors with confidence metadata.
Represent the Sakarya valley and Geyve–Mekece–Lefke corridor as route/frontier evidence, not as an invented smooth border.
Keep fortifications, roads, settlements and political control in separate layers.
Do not promote exact canonical province polygons until geometry-specific evidence and topology reconciliation are complete.
